clue.text: Made concessions for deal without repeat order included

indicators.note: without tells us to take the following letters out of the longer word

parts.note: to make concessions so as to reach a deal is to compromise; past tense to match 'Made'
OM is the Order of Merit; it is a repeat because those two letters already appear earlier in the word

explanation.surface: A negotiator gave ground to secure a deal, without a further order being included.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' removes the second OM (Order of Merit, the 'repeat' of the first) from COMPROMISED.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something comprised in a whole is contained or included in it.

clue.text: Infection amid lay congregation undermining church

indicators.note: in a down clue, undermining puts the jumbled letters beneath the church abbreviation
a congregation gathers people together, here gathering the letters of amid lay into a new order

explanation.surface: A disease spreads among the lay worshippers, sapping the church's strength.
explanation.walkthrough: 'congregation' turns AMID LAY into LAMYDIA, and 'undermining' sets that below CH in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a common sexually transmitted bacterial disease is one kind of infection.

clue.text: Paper report of thriller, here?

indicators.note: a report is something heard, so the word that follows is to be spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: the Thrilla in Manila was the 1975 Ali v Frazier fight, so the capital of the Philippines is where that thriller took place

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a newspaper's account of a gripping story is in this edition.
explanation.walkthrough: The theme is Muhammad Ali: his third bout with Joe Frazier was billed 'the Thrilla in Manila'.
explanation.definitionFit: Manilla is a strong brown paper used for envelopes and folders, once made from Manila hemp.

clue.text: Moan when missing opening fight in Vegas

indicators.note: missing opening tells us the first letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: to moan is to grumble

explanation.surface: Someone complains after missing the start of a big Las Vegas boxing match.
explanation.walkthrough: Ali fought several times in Las Vegas, and 'rumble' is American slang for a street fight.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang synonym: in American usage a rumble is a brawl or gang fight.

clue.text: Post card, perhaps, where ultimately no love's lost within

indicators.note: within means those letters are set inside the card's abbreviation

parts.note: an SD card is a memory card used in cameras and phones

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word before it
lost means the letter standing for love goes missing from the word

parts.note: love is zero in tennis scoring, the letter O

explanation.surface: Sending a greeting card to someone you have no affection for.
explanation.walkthrough: 'card, perhaps' is not a postcard but an SD memory card. 'ultimately' gives E, 'lost' takes O from NO, and 'within' puts E + N inside SD.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to post a letter is to dispatch it by mail.

clue.text: Field event one's put up on review

parts.note: the discus is an athletics field event

indicators.note: in a down clue, put up means written upwards, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: one is I, and one's stands for 'one is', giving I and S

explanation.surface: An athletics event is being looked at again after a contested result.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one's' is read as 'one is' (I + IS shortened to IS), and 'put up' turns it to SI in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a review of a matter is a talking-over or consideration of it.

clue.text: First-class stout returned for Caribbean rum

indicators.note: returned means the letters are sent back the way they came, read right to left

parts.note: A1 means first-class, written AI with the figure one as the letter I
stout means fat

explanation.surface: A drinker sends back a top stout and asks for West Indian rum instead.
explanation.walkthrough: A1 (first-class) is written AI, the digit one standing in for the letter I; 'returned' reads the whole lot right to left.
explanation.definitionFit: Taffia or tafia is a cheap rum distilled in the West Indies from molasses or cane refuse.

clue.text: Bible opening leads to struggle

indicators.note: opening means splitting the other word apart to sit inside it

parts.note: a trail is a set of leads or signs to be followed
AV is the Authorised Version of the Bible

explanation.surface: Reading the start of the Bible sets someone off on a hard spiritual effort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'opening' looks like the start of the Bible, but it is the container signal: the Bible version splits the other word open.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: travail is painful, laborious effort or toil.

clue.text: Warning on course with staff supervisor

parts.note: golfers shout 'fore' on the course to warn of an incoming ball
to staff a post is to man it

explanation.surface: A golf club shouts a warning to its course workers and their boss.
explanation.walkthrough: George Foreman, beaten by Ali in Kinshasa in 1974, fits the boxing theme.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a foreman is the worker in charge who oversees a team.

clue.text: Given support, said we'd see who starts to leave

indicators.note: starts to leave tells us the opening letters of the two words drop away

explanation.surface: Someone helped out, saying they'd watch who began to drift away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starts to leave' removes the first letters S and W from SAID and WE'D, leaving AID + ED.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to be aided is to have been helped or assisted.

clue.text: Menial exercises followed by new railway worker

indicators.note: exercises suggests putting the letters through their paces into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A lowly worker does exercises before a newcomer joins the railway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exercises' is the anagram signal; 'Menial' looks like a description of the worker but is the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A lineman is a person employed to inspect and maintain railway track or signal lines.

clue.text: Boxed supermarket wine

parts.note: Spar is a chain of supermarkets and convenience shops
red is a type of wine

explanation.surface: A shopper picks up a cheap box of supermarket wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boxed' reads as packaged wine but is the past tense of fighting with fists, in keeping with the boxing theme.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to have sparred is to have boxed, especially in practice.

clue.text: Slightly left in dark over Libya's domain code

indicators.note: in tells us the abbreviation for left sits inside the other word
over means turned over, so the word for dark is read backwards

parts.note: dark means dim
web addresses in Libya end in .ly

explanation.surface: Someone is a bit puzzled, left in the dark about Libya's internet code.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns the word for dark round to MID, and 'in' places L inside it to give MILD.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to do something mildly is to do it to a small degree.

clue.text: Clay probed by amateur graduate leading to Area 51 legend?

indicators.note: leading to means the first part comes before what follows
probed by means the word for clay has the others pushed inside it

parts.note: clay is wet earth, or mud
a ham is an amateur, as in a radio ham
MA, Master of Arts, is a graduate
51 in Roman numerals is LI

explanation.surface: A ufologist's tale: some clay is examined by an amateur graduate, pointing to the Area 51 myth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clay' tempts as the definition, since the boxer was born Cassius Clay, but it is wordplay; 'probed by' and 'leading to' do the assembly.
explanation.definitionFit: The boxer who called himself 'the Greatest' is a sporting legend.

clue.text: Trailer for Hansel and Gretel?

parts.note: not a film preview: in the fairy tale the children lay a trail of crumbs to find their way home

explanation.surface: Someone asks about the preview for a film of the fairy tale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trailer' suggests a cinema preview; here it is something used to lay a trail through the forest.
explanation.definitionFit: Hansel dropped crumbs of bread along the path, each one a marker of their trail.

clue.text: Dull spot around Reading, for example

indicators.note: around means the word for spot is wrapped round the other letter

parts.note: a dab is a small spot of something
reading is one of the three Rs (reading, writing, arithmetic), so R

explanation.surface: Someone finds a dreary place in or near the town of Reading.
explanation.walkthrough: Reading is a Berkshire town, but here it is one of 'the three Rs' of basic education, giving R.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: drab means dull, lacking colour or interest.

clue.text: BT's first mobile network — one creating a buzz

indicators.note: first picks out the opening letter of the company name

parts.note: EE is a UK mobile phone network

explanation.surface: A telecoms headline: BT's leading mobile network is generating excitement.
explanation.walkthrough: BT is the British telecoms company and EE a UK mobile network it owns.
explanation.definitionFit: A bee buzzes as it flies, so it is an insect making a humming sound; Ali would 'sting like a bee'.

clue.text: 'Pastures new' welcomed by boys on marijuana

indicators.note: on means the second part comes after the first in this across entry

parts.note: grass is slang for marijuana

indicators.note: welcomed by means taken inside the word for boys

parts.note: lads are boys

explanation.surface: Stoned young men head off for fresh fields, quoting Milton's 'pastures new'.
explanation.walkthrough: 'welcomed by' places N inside the word for boys, making LANDS; 'on' puts that after the drug.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: pastures are fields of grass used for grazing.

clue.text: See 12
Song more fancy than essay

indicators.note: made more fancy, the letters are dressed up in a new order

explanation.surface: A comment that a song is more elaborate than an essay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'more fancy' rearranges THAN ESSAY.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a work song sung by sailors is one kind of song.

clue.text: Current provider's key rate on supply meeting resistance

parts.note: Alt is a key on a computer keyboard

indicators.note: supply here is an adverb, in a supple or flexible way, so the letters bend into a new order

parts.note: R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: An electricity supplier's key tariff is set against public resistance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supply' looks like a noun but is read as 'in a supple way', rearranging RATE ON into ERNATO.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: a device generating alternating electric current is a provider of current.

clue.text: Fighter having rent trouble

parts.note: rent is a past form of rend, meaning torn
ado is fuss or trouble

explanation.surface: A boxer is having difficulties paying the rent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rent' looks like money for housing; here it means torn.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the Panavia Tornado is a military fighter jet.

clue.text: Growth mum's neglected? It may be hard to swallow

indicators.note: neglected means those letters are left out

parts.note: a shrubbery is a growth of bushes
mum means silent, and SH is the call for silence

explanation.surface: Garden growth Mum hasn't tended, and something not easily believed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mum' is not mother but 'keep quiet', SH, which is removed from SHRUBBERY.
explanation.definitionFit: Tough, chewy food has a texture like tyre material and is difficult to get down.

clue.text: Plan inside army barracks

indicators.note: barracks here is a verb, houses, so the words hold the answer within them

explanation.surface: A scheme is being hatched inside the army barracks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'barracks' looks like the army's quarters but is a verb meaning 'houses', and INSIDE ARMY houses the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an idea can be a plan or scheme in mind.

clue.text: Take off pants, say, to gather information

parts.note: the prefix de- means taking off or removing
briefs are an example of pants, or underwear

explanation.surface: An undressing instruction that turns into an intelligence-gathering session.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as 'remove the underpants'; DE- signals removal, and BRIEF is underwear.
explanation.definitionFit: To debrief someone is to question them after a mission to obtain information.

clue.text: 90s music from Amazon?

definitions.meaning: a style of fast breakbeat dance music popular in the 1990s
the Amazon basin is a vast rainforest, an example of dense tropical forest

explanation.surface: Someone asks if 1990s dance music can be bought from the online retailer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Amazon' suggests the online shop, but it is the rainforest; Ali's Rumble in the ___ was in Zaire.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: a 90s dance genre and the dense tropical forest of the Amazon.

clue.text: Book hotel and a second on way

indicators.note: on means the next piece comes after the previous one in this across entry

parts.note: H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet
RD is the abbreviation for road, a way
to second a proposal is to back it

explanation.surface: A traveller reserves a hotel and a quick second stop along the route.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Book' looks like a verb meaning reserve; it is the noun, a hardbound volume.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a book bound in stiff covers is one kind of book.

clue.text: Cuts cash outlay, saving grand

indicators.note: saving means keeping within, so the other letter is held inside
outlay read as laid out, setting the letters out differently

parts.note: a grand is a thousand pounds, K

explanation.surface: A firm reduces spending but holds onto a thousand pounds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outlay' turns CASH into HACS, and 'saving' holds K inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to hack something is to cut it roughly.

clue.text: Muslim attire leaders of Jaipur used, before burkas achieved hegemony

indicators.note: leaders of means the opening letter of each following word

explanation.surface: Indian city leaders dressed in a certain way before the burka became dominant.
explanation.walkthrough: Jaipur is a city in Rajasthan, India.
explanation.definitionFit: A jubbah is a long loose outer garment worn by Muslim men.

clue.text: Sent charge on time

indicators.note: on means the second piece follows the first

parts.note: a rap is a criminal charge, as in 'beat the rap'

explanation.surface: A charge was sent out on time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sent' is not dispatched but the slang sense, thrilled or enraptured.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang synonym: to be sent is to be carried away with delight, utterly absorbed.

clue.text: Gold on cheap feathered hat

indicators.note: on means the gold symbol follows
feathered suggests ruffled, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: AU is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: A gold trim adorns a cheap hat with feathers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'feathered' looks like it describes the hat but ruffles CHEAP into CHAPE.
explanation.definitionFit: Chapeau is the French word for a hat, used in English too.

clue.text: Old Ford model with name of German heritage

definitions.note: an adjective phrase, matching the adjective answer

parts.note: the Ford Anglia was a British family car made from 1939 to 1967

explanation.surface: A vintage Ford whose name has German origins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old Ford model' looks like the definition, but it is the wordplay ANGLIA.
explanation.definitionFit: The Angles were a Germanic people who settled eastern England, so an East Anglian belongs to that heritage.

clue.text: Sound level in audiobook, maybe

indicators.note: sound here means the word is spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: a storey is a level of a building

explanation.surface: A comment about volume settings when listening to an audiobook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound level' reads as volume; 'Sound' is the homophone signal and 'level' a floor of a building.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: an audiobook is a narrative or tale read aloud.

clue.text: Cut of meat?

parts.note: a joint split open and flattened is a butchery style, and the question mark nods to Ali, who could 'float like' this insect

explanation.surface: A butcher is asked about a particular way of preparing meat.
explanation.walkthrough: Butterflied meat is split and opened flat; Ali boasted he would 'float like a butterfly, sting like a bee'.
explanation.definitionFit: A butterfly cut is a joint split almost through and opened out flat, resembling wings.
